Quote.body: Woman is born free and lives equal to man in her rights.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 1 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: Man, are you capable of being just? It is a woman who poses the question.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: Social distinctions can be based only on the common utility.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 1 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: After bread, education is the first need of the people.
Quote.author: Georges Danton

Quote.body: Audacity, audacity, and again audacity.
Quote.author: Georges Danton

Quote.body: You cannot take your country with you on the soles of your shoes.
Quote.author: Georges Danton

Quote.body: The secret of freedom lies in educating people.
Quote.author: Maximilien Robespierre

Quote.body: The secret of tyranny is in keeping them ignorant.
Quote.author: Maximilien Robespierre

Quote.body: Louis must die, because the homeland has to live.
Quote.author: Maximilien Robespierre

Quote.body: No one loves armed missionaries.
Quote.author: Maximilien Robespierre

Quote.body: Liberty consists in the freedom to do everything which injures no one else.
Quote.author: Marquis de Lafayette

Quote.body: Humanity has gained its suit; Liberty will nevermore be without an asylum.
Quote.author: Marquis de Lafayette

Quote.body: The law must be the same for all, whether it protects or punishes.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 6 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Men are born and remain free and equal in rights.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 1 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: The aim of every political association is the preservation of rights.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 2 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Liberty, equality, fraternity.
Quote.author: French Revolutionary Motto

Quote.body: Citizens, the homeland is in danger.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: He who trembles at this moment is guilty.
Quote.author: Louis Antoine de Saint-Just

Quote.body: No one can reign innocently.
Quote.author: Louis Antoine de Saint-Just

Quote.body: Happiness is a new idea in Europe.
Quote.author: Louis Antoine de Saint-Just

Quote.body: When government violates the rights of the people, insurrection is a sacred right and duty.
Quote.author: French National Convention

Quote.body: The principle of all sovereignty resides essentially in the nation.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 3 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Freedom consists in being able to do anything that does not harm others.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 4 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: No person shall be accused, arrested, or imprisoned except according to law.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 7 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: The free communication of ideas and opinions is one of the most precious rights of man.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 11 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: All citizens are equally eligible to all dignities, places and public employments.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 6 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Property being an inviolable and sacred right, no one shall be deprived thereof except where public necessity demands.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 17 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: A society in which rights are not secured nor separation of powers established has no constitution.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 16 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: The law has the right to forbid only actions harmful to society.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 5 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: No one shall be disquieted on account of his opinions, including religious views.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 10 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: A common contribution is essential for maintenance of the public force and administration.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 13 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Citizens have the right to verify the necessity of public taxation and to monitor its use.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 14 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Society has the right to require every public agent to account for his administration.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 15 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: The source of all sovereignty resides essentially in the nation.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 3 (variant translation, 1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Liberty consists in the power to do whatever does not injure another.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 4 (variant translation, 1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: The social aim of all political institutions is the preservation of the natural rights of man.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: The exercise of the natural rights of each man has no limits except those that secure to others the enjoyment of these same rights.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: Anything not forbidden by law cannot be impeded.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: Law is the expression of the general will.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: The law should establish only penalties that are strictly and obviously necessary.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: A common contribution is essential for the maintenance of the public force.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: All citizens have the right to decide, either personally or by their representatives, as to the necessity of the public contribution.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: Society has the right to require of every public agent an account of his administration.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: Any society in which no provision is made for guaranteeing rights or separation of powers has no constitution.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: Property is an inviolable and sacred right.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: Freedom consists in the power to do whatever does not injure another.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: Citizens, there is no freedom for the enemies of freedom.
Quote.author: Louis Antoine de Saint-Just

Quote.body: The force of circumstances perhaps leads us to results we have not foreseen.
Quote.author: Camille Desmoulins

Quote.body: No person shall be disquieted on account of his opinions, including religious views.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: Ignorance, neglect, or contempt of the rights of man are the sole causes of public misfortunes.
Quote.author: French National Assembly

Quote.body: If woman has the right to mount the scaffold, she must equally have the right to mount the rostrum.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Postscript (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: Marriage is the tomb of trust and love.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Postscript (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: The purpose of all political association is the preservation of the natural rights of woman and man.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 2 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: The principle of all sovereignty resides essentially in the nation, which is only the union of woman and man.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 3 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: Liberty and justice consist in restoring all that belongs to others.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 4 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: The law ought to be the expression of the general will.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 6 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: All female and male citizens must contribute personally or through their representatives to its formation.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 6 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: No woman is exempt; she is accused, arrested, and detained in the cases determined by law.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 7 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: No one shall be disquieted on account of her opinions.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 10 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: Free communication of thoughts and opinions is one of the most precious rights of woman.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 11 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: The guarantee of the rights of woman and citizen requires public utilities.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 12 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: For the maintenance of the public force and the expenses of administration, the contributions of woman and man are equal.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 13 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: Women have the right to verify, by themselves or by their representatives, the necessity of the public contribution.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 14 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: The Constitution is null if the majority of the individuals composing the nation have not cooperated in drafting it.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 16 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: Property belongs to both sexes united or separated.
Quote.author: Olympe de Gouges
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Woman, Art. 17 (1791) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Olympe_de_Gouges

Quote.body: We must dare, and again dare, and go on daring.
Quote.author: Georges Danton

Quote.body: It is satisfying, for ministers of a free people, to be able to announce to them that the fatherland is going to be saved.
Quote.author: Georges Danton

Quote.body: Tomorrow I shall sleep in glory.
Quote.author: Georges Danton

Quote.body: Without virtue, terror is fatal; without terror, virtue is powerless.
Quote.author: Maximilien Robespierre

Quote.body: Terror is nothing other than justice, prompt, severe, inflexible.
Quote.author: Maximilien Robespierre

Quote.body: The goal of constitutional government is to preserve the republic; the goal of revolutionary government is to found it.
Quote.author: Maximilien Robespierre

Quote.body: The first maxim of your policy ought to be to lead the people by reason.
Quote.author: Maximilien Robespierre

Quote.body: Those who make revolution halfway only dig their own graves.
Quote.author: Louis Antoine de Saint-Just

Quote.body: Force, reason, and the people: one can only advance by these.
Quote.author: Louis Antoine de Saint-Just

Quote.body: Order today is the disorder of yesterday.
Quote.author: Louis Antoine de Saint-Just

Quote.body: We are here by the will of the people.
Quote.author: Honoré Gabriel Riqueti, comte de Mirabeau

Quote.body: Go tell your master that we are here by the will of the people and will leave only by the force of bayonets.
Quote.author: Honoré Gabriel Riqueti, comte de Mirabeau

Quote.body: Enjoy your life without comparing it with that of another.
Quote.author: Marquis de Condorcet

Quote.body: Either no individual of the human race has true rights, or all have the same.
Quote.author: Marquis de Condorcet
Quote.attribution: On the Admission of Women to the Rights of Citizenship (1790) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Marquis_de_Condorcet

Quote.body: O Liberty, what crimes are committed in thy name!
Quote.author: Madame Roland

Quote.body: What is the Third Estate? Everything.
Quote.author: Emmanuel Joseph Sieyès

Quote.body: What has it been until now in the political order? Nothing.
Quote.author: Emmanuel Joseph Sieyès

Quote.body: What does it demand? To become something.
Quote.author: Emmanuel Joseph Sieyès

Quote.body: The aim of society is the common happiness.
Quote.author: French National Convention

Quote.body: Resistance to oppression is a natural and imprescriptible right.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 2 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Government is instituted to guarantee to man the enjoyment of his natural and imprescriptible rights.
Quote.author: French National Convention

Quote.body: Public offices are essentially temporary; they can neither be considered rewards nor property.
Quote.author: French National Convention

Quote.body: A common contribution is essential for the maintenance of the public forces.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 13 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Instruction is the need of all. Society owes public reason to all its members.
Quote.author: French National Convention

Quote.body: Any society in which the guarantee of rights is not assured has no constitution.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 16 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Public force is instituted for the advantage of all, and not for the particular utility of those to whom it is entrusted.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 12 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: All citizens have the right to verify, by themselves or by their representatives, the necessity of public contributions.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 14 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: No one should be disturbed on account of his opinions, including his religious views.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 10 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Those who solicit, expedite, execute, or cause arbitrary orders to be executed ought to be punished.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 7 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: All severity not necessary to secure a person should be severely repressed by law.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 9 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: The limits of liberty can be determined only by law.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 4 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Any citizen may therefore speak, write, and print freely.
Quote.author: French National Assembly
Quote.attribution: Declaration of the Rights of Man, Art. 11 (1789) | https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Rights_of_Man_and_of_the_Citizen

Quote.body: Victory belongs to the most persevering.
Quote.author: Napoleon Bonaparte

Quote.body: Courage is like love; it must have hope to nourish it.
Quote.author: Napoleon Bonaparte

Quote.body: Imagination rules the world.
Quote.author: Napoleon Bonaparte
